name: backorders die honestly, and overpayment goes home
notes: INV-7 (the open quantity is the record of what is owed), INV-8, INV-20 (closure derived). close_short, the backorder view, and refunding unapplied cash.

steps.notes: INV-6: never silently reduce the ordered quantity — ship what exists and keep the remainder visible
INV-7: the 7 open units ARE the record that Proseware is still owed. This view is where backorders wait for fulfilment or an honest death

args.reason: item discontinued by supplier; customer notified and agreed

steps.notes: the honest death: the debt of goods is extinguished with a reason, committed credit exposure is released
INV-4 and INV-20: billed for the 5 fulfilled, never the 12 ordered — and with nothing open and everything billed, closure derives itself
the customer paid against the original order value — overpayment is real life, not an error state
omitted amount applies the smaller remaining side; the extra $375 stays as unapplied cash, visible (INV-8)
INV-17: bounded and the refusal names the bound — you cannot refund money that already settled an invoice
records that the money went back; actually moving it is out of scope, like every outbound act
clean end state: nothing owed in goods, nothing owed in cash, and every step of getting here is in the log
